explanation: Fires on the second digit of a two-digit number that starts with 2 (as in 24, 22, 28, 21), above all ages, days of the month, hours and '24 hours'. It fires moderately on inner digits of longer numbers such as years (19xx, 20xx) or page numbers, and weakly on other digits.

Mostly fires on ' of' in institution names ('Society of', 'School of', 'National Association of'). It also fires on a scattered set of other tokens: ' were' after a plural subject in scientific prose, 'personal' in 'personal computer', '-old', ' flight' and others. There is no clear rule beyond the ' of' cases.

Fires on 'See'/' see' used as a cross-reference instruction ('See also', 'Please see our Privacy Notice', 'See the ...'), plus ' (' before a parenthetical. The other strong hits are unrelated tokens in mid-sentence (' this', ',', ' be', ' has', code whitespace), so this is a mixture.

Fires on a wide, unrelated range of tokens: word-internal pieces, punctuation in code and IP addresses, ' at' in stack traces, 'v.' in case captions, ' State' in 'State of', ' to' in 'signal to noise', and others. No common context is visible.

Fires on the first part of a hyphenated compound or modifier, before a contrasting or complementary term ('HLA' in HLA-class or HLA-DRB, 'off'-resonant, 'non'-minority, 'dry' granules, 'allergic' disorders). It also fires on assorted other tokens, such as code braces and ' your' or ' the' in noun phrases.

Fires on verbs (and some nouns) that follow an auxiliary, negation or preposition in the middle of a clause: 'grew', 'posted' in 'haven't posted', 'listen' in 'did not listen', 'cry' in 'shoulder to cry on', 'walking' in 'within walking distance', 'the content of which'. In practice it is a broad, diffuse response to content words that carry the predicate.

Fires on ' how' (and ' way' or ' where') after expressions of uncertainty or seeking ('not sure how', 'how to address', 'haven't found a way'). It also fires on the first token of a name or identifier right after its introduction ('warn', 'Jay', 'Pen', 'android', 'api').

Fires on a heterogeneous mix of tokens: the second piece of a word or identifier ('Arizon|ans', 'Random|Forest', 'transist|ors'), number words such as ' two' and ' three', HTML tags and attribute values, and digits in IDs. There is no unifying context.

Fires on many different tokens without a shared theme: verbs after 'instead of', 'Below', the ' {' after a class declaration, "'t" in "don't" or "can't", ' which' or ' where' starting relative clauses, and ' a' before 'variety' or 'multitude'. This looks like a mixture of unrelated functions.

Fires on words for the people or users a service benefits, or on their experience, in mission-statement, customer-service or policy text: 'your experience', 'support for patients', 'harms consumers', 'many people', 'total satisfaction', 'survivors'. It fires most strongly on 'experience' in cookie or website notices, and weakly elsewhere.

Fires on content words (participles, verbs, adjectives, nouns) that come right after a determiner or noun in mid-sentence ('captured', 'visit', 'built around', 'geographical', 'birthday', 'married'). It shows no clear semantic selectivity, so the response is diffuse.

Fires on the first digit '1' of a four-digit year after 'in' or a date, especially in founding or first-description phrases ('founded in 1954', 'first described in 1946'), as well as on birth dates in biographies. It also fires on the '9' in '19xx'. Other dates fire moderately, and non-year numbers fire weakly.

Fires on word-final or word-internal subword pieces of technical, medical or chemical terms ('Methad|one', 'separ|in', 'op|iod|s', 'tachy|kin|ins', 'antitryps|in'). It also fires on some casual-speech tokens ('Shh', 'f-cking', ':D', 'say'), so the picture is mixed.

Fires on purpose or causative verbs after 'to' ('to bring an end', 'strive to make', 'toward bringing', 'to put into effect', 'to make money'). It also fires on unrelated tokens such as the ':' in clock times, 'x' in '4x100', 'typename' and include paths.

Fires on a mixture: the end of an acronym or a closing parenthesis inside a parenthetical abbreviation ('(DCT)', 'MoAbs', 'ddI)'), the variable term after '*' in algebra ('*f', '*b'), ' extends' in class declarations, and assorted function words.

Fires on a mixture: ' at' in the Boost license boilerplate ('copy at http'), '="' after layout_width in Android XML, '-' in CSS class names such as 'col-md-6', and auxiliary verbs or ' to' in 'be able to' or 'you are using'. These look like several unrelated contexts.

Fires in first-person or emotional statements about capability, expectation or imagination, on the verb or noun that completes the idea: 'keeping track', 'could have dared to imagine', 'everything I could', 'hard to imagine', 'never thought', 'no idea', "can't". Tokens elsewhere fire weakly.

Fires on the first subword token of a rare or foreign proper name or word that is split into pieces ('V|opak', 'Kos|kinen', 'M|ESS|ER', 'Mil|pitas', 'res|veratrol', 'res|umes'), especially capitalized name fragments. Common whole words do not make it fire.

Fires mostly in scientific or technical text, on list commas, ' by' after a method verb ('determined by', 'isolated by'), '%' in '95% CI', and on code punctuation (' /' flags, '.' method chains, ':'). It looks like a broad mixture of tokens related to technical text structure.

Fires on 'There'/' there' starting an existential clause ('There are', 'there is a lack of'), especially at the start of a sentence after a contrast. It also fires on tokens that follow a negation or restriction ('without', 'unless', 'not limited to', 'bad news').

Fires on ' how' in 'no matter how' or 'doesn't matter how' (the strongest case), and on ' since' as a temporal conjunction. It also fires on the first piece of split words such as 'cul|minate', 'ser|pentine' and '-c|oping', so the set is a mixture.
